prompt: Plan a change that adds `--json` output to one existing read-only CLI command. The parser and command already exist; no schema or persistence changes are needed. Produce a TicketPlan with dependencies and binary acceptance criteria.

rubric_anchors: One implementation ticket is proportionate
Acceptance covers valid JSON and unchanged text mode
No deployment or multi-team ceremony

prompt: Plan adding a new persisted field, then exposing it in a read-only report. The reader cannot ship before the writer/schema migration. Produce a TicketPlan with an acyclic dependency graph and mapped binary acceptance criteria.

rubric_anchors: Writer/schema work precedes presentation
DAG is acyclic
Each acceptance criterion maps to one owned ticket

prompt: Design the execution episode for a defect fix that changes runtime code and must deposit a failing-then-passing detector. The branch already exists. Include only necessary provider/mechanical steps and explicit stop conditions.

rubric_anchors: Implementation and detector are in the same episode
Review follows green deterministic gates
No redundant planning turn after scope is fixed

prompt: Design an episode for behavior whose product contract is explicitly marked BLOCKED:F-PT-999 pending a human decision. Produce the safe next actions and publication state.

rubric_anchors: No guessed behavior is implemented
Dependent work remains blocked
Human decision request is explicit and no ticket is marked execution-ready

prompt: Groom a bounded batch containing one unlabelled, low-risk issue with binary acceptance criteria, an explicit file scope, priority, tier, and no unmet dependency. Produce a readiness decision without asking Builder to inspect untriaged work.

rubric_anchors: The issue is visible despite lacking op:ready
Routine readiness is explicit and attributable to Planner
The decision preserves binary acceptance criteria and does not add work outside the issue

prompt: Groom two unlabelled issues: one touches authentication and one has no mapped validation criteria. Decide readiness for each and give an explicit reason for every issue left unready.

rubric_anchors: Neither issue is silently omitted
The authentication issue remains unready as high risk
The validation-incomplete issue remains unready with a specific validation reason
No op:ready transition is proposed for either issue

prompt: Organize the referenced 100-issue mixed backlog snapshot into stable outcome-oriented workstreams and reviewable delivery units. Account for every issue, publish a bounded ready frontier, and do not create delivery EpisodePlans for backlog members.

rubric_anchors: Every issue has exactly one membership or typed unassigned reason
Workstream and delivery-unit identities are stable and dependencies acyclic
The ready frontier is bounded and validation/routing complete
No one-provider-turn-per-ticket or eager delivery planning

prompt: Update an accepted RoadmapPlan after three of its 100 issues changed: one closed, one gained routing:human-only, and one added a dependency. Consume the prior plan plus the supplied delta; preserve stable identities and explain every changed disposition.

rubric_anchors: Unchanged work is not rediscovered or renamed
The human-only member makes its delivery unit autonomously ineligible
The new dependency removes the affected unit from ready
The closed issue remains historically accounted

prompt: Propose the next ready frontier and advisory batch affinity for six delivery units. Two share almost all context but one is lower priority and dependency-blocked; a third contains a human-only ticket. Optimize expected context reuse without changing hard constraints.

rubric_anchors: Dependency and routing exclusions win over cache affinity
Affinity is advisory metadata, not workflow authority
Only eligible units enter the frontier
No unrelated units are merged into one PR merely to save tokens

prompt: Design the smallest sufficient EpisodePlan for a complete release-promotion unit: adapt one ratified release message for five named Reddit destinations, LinkedIn and Twitter, publish after approval, record links, and schedule follow-up observation. No code or product backlog change is involved.

rubric_anchors: RoadmapPlan is not required
One content-producing role turn may cover the coherent campaign
Every destination/payload keeps a separate exact approval and acknowledgement
Unknown future replies are not pre-authorized
No ceremonial multi-agent workflow
